title: Fall of Acre to the Mamluks
summary: Mamluk forces under Sultan al-Ashraf Khalil broke into Acre on 18 May 1291 after a siege that began in April. A massacre followed, and survivors were killed, evacuated or sold into slavery; the Templars held the south-west quarter about ten more days and the captured Templars were executed. Sidon, Tyre, Beirut, Tortosa and Athlit fell by August; the military orders moved to Cyprus.

uncertainty.note: Day-level date from World History Encyclopedia; EBSCO gives the year only. The siege start is given as 6 April 1291 by World History Encyclopedia.

where.historical_name: Acre, the main Christian-held port in the Levant, in the Kingdom of Jerusalem under King Henry of Cyprus-Jerusalem

importance.justification: The loss of Acre ended the main crusader foothold on the Levant coast and shifted the military orders to Cyprus.

audience_note: Describes a massacre of civilians and the enslavement of survivors following the capture of a city.

related.because: EBSCO says that after Ain Jalut the surrounded Crusader strongholds were captured one by one by the Mamluks between 1263 and 1291, ending with Acre.

reviewer_note: The day-level date rests on one opened page (World History Encyclopedia); EBSCO confirms only 1291. Neither page gives death or captive figures, so none is stated. The summary says only April for the siege start because other web accounts say 5 April.
